stories.hook: ¿Puede la ketamina mejorar la memoria de trabajo en depresión?
stories.headline: Ketamina reduce síntomas depresivos sin afectar desempeño en tarea de memoria
stories.finding: En un ensayo cruzado, doble ciego, la ketamina (0,5 mg/kg) redujo significativamente la puntuación del MADRS frente al placebo (p < 0,01) en 22 pacientes con depresión resistente. El desempeño en la tarea N‑back se mantuvo, y el ROI mostró menor activación del giro temporal superior en pacientes versus controles (p < 0,01).
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que la ketamina puede aliviar rápidamente la depresión resistente sin deteriorar la memoria de trabajo, lo que apoya su uso clínico y orienta investigaciones sobre los circuitos neurales implicados.
stories.paperTitle: Working memory neural correlates after ketamine in treatment-resistant depression: a randomized placebo-controlled functional magnetic resonance imaging study
stories.originalAbstract: Ketamine exerts rapid antidepressant effects in treatment-resistant depression (TRD), but its impact on working memory and neural circuitry remains unclear. This secondary analysis investigated behavioral and neural changes during a working memory task post-ketamine infusion in TRD participants versus healthy volunteers (HVs). Data were previously collected from a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover trial of 22 unmedicated TRD participants (14F/8 M) and 19 matched HVs (12F/7 M). Participants received ketamine (0.5mg/kg) and placebo two weeks apart. 3T fMRI was acquired during an N-back task at baseline and two days post-ketamine. Accuracy, reaction time, and differential neural activation during 3-back versus 1-back contrasts were analyzed. Ketamine significantly reduced Montgomery-Asberg Depression Rating Scale scores compared to placebo (p < 0.01). N-back task performance did not significantly differ between drug conditions. In region of interest (ROI) analyses, TRD participants showed reduced activation in the superior temporal gyrus versus HVs (p < 0.01) after both infusions, and both groups demonstrated decreased parieto-occipital junction activation post-ketamine versus post-placebo (p = 0.01). Baseline dorsolateral prefrontal cortex activity significantly predicted post-infusion activity (p < 0.01). Ketamine's antidepressant effects occurred without significant changes in working memory performance, though region-specific task-related brain changes were observed. Interpretation is limited by modest sample size and the exploratory nature of the ROI analyses. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: www.clinicaltrials.gov, NCT00088699.

stories.hook: ¿Por qué la autocrítica impulsa la procrastinación académica?
stories.headline: La rumiación autocrítica media entre perfeccionismo y procrastinación
stories.finding: El estudio validó la Escala de Rumiación Autocrítica en turco con 282 estudiantes, demostrando buena fiabilidad y validez. En una muestra de 712 universitarios, la rumiación autocrítica medió significativamente la relación entre perfeccionismo desadaptativo y procrastinación académica.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que intervenir la rumiación autocrítica podría reducir la procrastinación en estudiantes perfeccionistas, ofreciendo una diana terapéutica para mejorar el rendimiento académico y el bienestar.
stories.paperTitle: Öz Eleştirel Ruminasyon Ölçeğinin Psikometrik Özelliklerinin İncelenmesi ve Üniversite Öğrencilerindeki Mükemmeliyetçilik ile Akademik Erteleme İlişkilerinde Öz Eleştirel Ruminasyonun Aracılık Rolü
stories.originalAbstract: Bu araştırmanın amacı Öz Eleştirel Ruminasyon Ölçeğinin Türk kültüründeki psikometrik özelliklerini ortaya koymak ve üniversite öğrencilerinin mükemmeliyetçilik ile akademik erteleme davranışları arasındaki ilişkide öz eleştirel ruminasyonun aracılık rolünün incelemektir. Bu amaç doğrultusunda ilk olarak 2018-2019 Eğitim Öğretim yılı Güz döneminde Muğla Sıtkı Koçman Üniversitesinde öğrenim gören 282 lisans öğrencisine ulaşılmıştır. Elde edilen veriler doğrultusunda Doğrulayıcı Faktör Analizi yapılmıştır. Yapılan geçerlik ve güvenirlik analizleri sonucunda Öz Eleştirel Ruminasyon Ölçeğinin Türk kültüründe geçerli ve güvenilir bir ölçme aracı olduğu sonucuna varılmıştır. Ardından mükemmeliyetçilik, öz eleştirel ruminasyon ve akademik erteleme davranışı arasındaki ilişkiyi incelemek ve öz eleştirel ruminasyonun aracılık rolünü ortaya koymak amacıyla yaşları 18 ile 33 arasında değişen 712 lisans öğrencisine ölçek uygulaması yapılmıştır. Elde edilen verilerle Basit Aracılık Analizi yapılmıştır. Verilerin analizinde Jamovi ve RStudio programlarından yararlanılmıştır. Elde edilen bulgulara göre uyumsuz mükemmeliyetçilik ile akademik erteleme davranışı arasındaki ilişkide öz eleştirel ruminasyonun tam aracı rolünün olduğu görülmüştür. Öte yandan uyumlu mükemmeliyetçilik ile akademik erteleme arasında düşük düzeyde negatif ve anlamlı bir ilişkinin olduğu görülürken öz eleştirel ruminasyon arasında anlamlı herhangi bir ilişkiye rastlanmamıştır. Son olarak elde edilen bulgular alanyazındaki çalışmalar doğrultusunda tartışılmış ve hem araştırmacılara hem de uygulayıcılara yönelik önerilerde bulunulmuştur.

stories.hook: ¿Cómo influye el peso al nacer en la ansiedad emprendedora?
stories.headline: Peso al nacer se asocia curvilinealmente con la tendencia a emprender, mediado por ansiedad
stories.finding: En tres muestras longitudinales de Finlandia, Reino Unido y EE. UU., y mediante regresiones de variables instrumentales y un estudio de gemelos, se halló una relación curvilineal entre el peso al nacer y la probabilidad de autoempleo. Además, los análisis respaldaron que la ansiedad medía dicha asociación.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que factores biológicos tempranos pueden predisponer a patrones de comportamiento empresarial a través de la ansiedad, lo que abre nuevas vías para intervenciones preventivas dirigidas a la regulación emocional desde la infancia.
stories.journal: Warwick Research Archive Portal (University of Warwick)
stories.originalAbstract: In this thesis, we adopt a four-paper framework to examine how biology relates to entrepreneurship. In the first paper, we conduct a systematic review of the literature on the biological perspective in management and investigate research spanning the areas of genetics, physiology and neuroscience. We present an organizing framework of the area, explain the mechanisms through which biological factors relate to management, and discuss the implications of the biological perspective. Finally, we present an agenda highlighting avenues for future research. In the second paper, we explore the association between birth weight and self-employment using three samples - two longitudinal datasets and a sample of twins - from Finland, the UK and the USA. After accounting for endogeneity with the use of longitudinal designs, two-stage least squares instrumental variable regressions and a twin study design, we find evidence for a curvilinear relationship between birth weight and the tendency to become self-employed. We propose a mediating psychological mechanism – anxiety – to explain this association and find support for this. In the third paper, we contribute to the literature linking mental conditions to entrepreneurship by exploring the relationship between anxiety and entrepreneurship using five samples – one cross sectional, three longitudinal and a sample of twins. We find a negative relationship between anxiety and the tendency to engage in entrepreneurship. Our findings also suggest that improving individuals’ financial conditions can attenuate the negative influence of anxiety on entrepreneurship. The fourth paper explores the relationship between breastfeeding duration and the likelihood of engaging in entrepreneurship using two longitudinal datasets from the UK. After partly mitigating endogeneity concerns using the Mundlak-Chamberlain estimator and two-stage least squares instrumental variable regression, we find a positive relationship between breastfeeding duration and the tendency to become an entrepreneur. We propose a mediating psychological mechanism – openness to experience – to explain this relationship.

stories.hook: ¿Puede un chatbot de IA mejorar la depresión universitaria?
stories.headline: Chatbot de IA basado en TCC reduce depresión y soledad en estudiantes chinos
stories.finding: En un ensayo controlado aleatorizado con 100 universitarios chinos (media 20,8 años), 50 recibieron un chatbot de IA basado en TCC durante 7 días y 50 fueron control de lista de espera. Se observaron interacciones significativas grupo×tiempo, indicando disminución de depresión, ansiedad y soledad en el grupo de intervención.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que intervenciones breves y automatizadas basadas en TCC pueden ser una herramienta eficaz y escalable para mitigar síntomas depresivos y de soledad en poblaciones universitarias bajo estrés financiero.
stories.paperTitle: Effect of a Cognitive Behavioral Therapy–Based AI Chatbot on Depression and Loneliness in Chinese University Students: Randomized Controlled Trial With Financial Stress Moderation
stories.originalAbstract: Background: Mental health concerns are prevalent among university students, with financial stress further compounding these issues. While cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is effective for these conditions, its delivery through artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots represents a promising approach, especially in non-Western contexts. Objective: This study aims to investigate the efficacy of a culturally adapted, CBT-based AI chatbot for improving the well-being of Chinese university students and to examine whether financial stress moderates its effectiveness. Methods: In this randomized controlled trial, 100 university students (mean age 20.8, SD 2.2 years; 62/100, 62% female) were allocated to either an intervention (n=50) or a waitlist control group (n=50). The intervention group interacted with a CBT-based AI chatbot for 7 consecutive days. Depression (Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale), anxiety (Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 scale), and loneliness (UCLA Loneliness Scale) were assessed at baseline, day 3, and day 7. Financial stress was measured using the Psychological Inventory of Financial Scarcity. Results: Significant group×time interactions were found for depression (F2,196=8.63; P<.001; η²p=.08) and loneliness (F2,196=5.57; P=.004; η²p=.05), but not for anxiety (F2,196=1.31; P=.27; η²p=.01). Post hoc comparisons showed significant reductions in both depression (t=3.85; P<.001) and loneliness (t=4.28; P<.001) from baseline to postintervention in the intervention group, with corresponding effect sizes of Cohen d=0.71 (95% CI 0.30-1.12) and Cohen d=0.60 (95% CI 0.20-1.00), respectively. No significant changes were observed in the waitlist control group. Exploratory subgroup analyses revealed that participants with high financial stress demonstrated significantly greater improvements in depression (F2,52=11.56; P<.001; η²p=.31) and loneliness (F2,52=11.18; P<.001; η²p=.30) compared to those with low financial stress. Conclusions: The culturally adapted, CBT-based AI chatbot effectively reduced depression and loneliness in Chinese university students, with stronger effects among those experiencing high financial stress. These findings highlight the potential of AI-driven interventions to provide accessible mental health support, particularly for financially stressed students.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la regulación emocional amortiguar el trauma infantil?
stories.headline: La regulación emocional media parcialmente el impacto del trauma infantil en síntomas internalizantes
stories.finding: En 100 adolescentes (13‑19 años), el trauma infantil se asoció con mayores dificultades de regulación emocional (r = 0.246, p < .05) y con síntomas internalizantes (r = 0.325, p < .01). La mediación parcial de la regulación emocional explicó parte del vínculo entre trauma y síntomas (B = 0.059, IC 95 % = 0.011‑…).
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que intervenir en la regulación emocional podría reducir los efectos del trauma infantil sobre la sintomatología internalizante, ofreciendo una vía terapéutica concreta para adolescentes en contextos clínicos.
stories.paperTitle: Childhood Trauma, Emotional Regulation, Alexithymia, and Psychological Symptoms Among Adolescents: A Mediational Analysis
stories.originalAbstract: Background: Adolescents’ mental health is influenced by childhood trauma, emotional regulation, and psychological symptoms. This study aimed to explore these interconnections among adolescents attending a child and adolescent clinic. Method: Adolescents aged 13-19 from a city were recruited through purposive sampling. Data were collected using the Child Behavior Checklist (CBCL), Childhood Trauma Questionnaire-Short Form (CTQ), Difficulties in Emotion Regulation Scale (DERS), and Toronto Alexithymia Scale-20. Adolescents with severe mental or physical illnesses were excluded. Results: A total of 100 participants were recruited aged 13-19. The CTQ scores positively correlated with DERS Scores ( r = 0.246, P < .05) and Internalizing scores ( r = 0.325, P < .01). DERS Scores strongly correlated with alexithymia ( r = 0.624, P < .001) and Internalizing scores( r = 0.556, P < .001). Regression analyses revealed CTQ, Alexithymia, and DERS scores significantly predicted Internalizing scores ( R 2 = 0.37). Mediation analysis showed that emotional regulation partially mediated the relationship between child trauma and Internalizing scores ( B = 0.059, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.011 to 0.133, t = 1.92, P = .01), as well as the relationship between Alexithymia and Internalizing scores( B = 0.255, 95% CI = 0.129 to 0.465, t = 3.31, P < .001). Conclusion: Findings highlight the importance of emotional regulation as a mediator in the connections between childhood trauma, alexithymia, and psychological symptoms among adolescents. This complementary mediation underscores the dual impact of direct and indirect effects on psychological well-being. The findings reveal intricate links between childhood trauma, emotional regulation, and alexithymia in adolescents with psychological symptoms. Emotional regulation proved to have a pivotal role in influencing psychological well-being. These results emphasize the importance of considering emotional regulation when assessing and maintaining mental health in adolescents, further contributing to understanding treatment needs.

stories.hook: ¿Por qué los estudiantes siguen a profesores narcisistas?
stories.headline: Validación del 'Efecto Stela' revela vínculo entre narcisismo y innovación educativa
stories.finding: De 1 045 cuestionarios (817 procesados; 779 estudiantes y 38 docentes) la validación mostró ítems con p < 0.001. Estos siguieron una curva sigmoidal alineada con la literatura sobre narcisismo brillante y oscuro, confirmando el 'Efecto Stela' como constructo medible del atractivo narcisista en contextos educativos.
stories.takeaway: Este instrumento permite identificar y gestionar la influencia del narcisismo docente sobre la innovación y el compromiso estudiantil, ofreciendo una base empírica para diseñar intervenciones que favorezcan relaciones pedagógicas más equilibradas.
stories.paperTitle: The "Stela Effect" of bright and dark narcissism on educational innovation in higher education: exploratory psychometric validation
stories.originalAbstract: Abstract In higher education, where we investigate emotional competencies, we displayed 1045 questionnaires, 817 of which were ultimately processed, with 779 students and 38 teachers from 9 architectural and engineering schools in Spain. We designed the Empathic Survey by asking teachers how they considered their students had answered to the questions. Thirty-eight variables were employed: 32 first-generation variables (22 operationalized emotion items and 10 sociodemographic items), 4 s-generation variables, and 2 third-generation variables. The second- and third-generation variables were inferred. We conducted an initial psychometric validation focused on reliability and internal structure. The results of the statistical analyses revealed several items with p-values less than 0.001. The values depict a sigmoidal shape whose interpretation fits with the literature about bright and dark narcissism. The Stela Effect name comes from the fact that it explains the behavior of students fascinated by teachers with narcissistic traits as if they were attracted to a comet tail. To contrast its meaning and coherence, as it is a graphic representation without antecedents, we present its correlations in various areas of knowledge and disciplines, such as Theory of Mind (ToM), Attachment, the Unconscious, Self-esteem, Dissociation, Shame, Empathy, Teaching, different aspects and approaches to Narcissism (continuous and dual) and its measurement, and the field of Contradictions. At the same time, we discuss its meaning from biases and different schools of psychological thought. We consider the Stela Effect the operationalization of a dual and dynamic model of narcissism sustained by several authors, and it helps us to understand many contradictions around narcissistic behavior. We conclude the presentation of the study in its current state with a practical implication: as an educational innovation, we propose using the Stela Effect framework as a pedagogical enhancement. Specifically, we outline a six-phase intervention protocol designed to help individuals develop awareness of their maladaptive tendencies and work through them, thereby transitioning toward more collaborative and effective modes of functioning.

stories.hook: ¿Por qué el trauma altera nuestro control emocional?
stories.headline: El trauma produce hiperreactividad amigdalar y disfunción del eje HPA
stories.finding: Los metaanálisis y estudios de neuroimagen en TEPT revelan hiperreactividad de la amígdala, hipocactivación del córtex prefrontal ventromedial y reducción del volumen hipocampal. Además, se observa un perfil de hipocortisolismo acompañado de hiperactivación simpática, retirada parasimpática y disminución de la variabilidad de la frecuencia cardíaca.
stories.takeaway: Comprender estos marcadores neurobiológicos permite diseñar intervenciones dirigidas a normalizar la actividad amigdalar y la regulación autonómica, mejorando la terapia de exposición y estrategias de regulación emocional en pacientes con TEPT.
stories.paperTitle: The Neurobiology of Trauma: From Threat Detection to Somatic Dysregulation
stories.originalAbstract: Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) represents the most extensively studied neurobiological sequela of traumatic experience. Within that scope, this chapter examines the neural circuitry underlying threat detection and fear regulation, hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal (HPA) axis dysregulation, autonomic nervous system dysfunction and its cardiovascular consequences, memory impairment, and the somatic manifestations of trauma. Meta-analytic and neuroimaging evidence consistently identifies amygdala hyperreactivity, ventromedial prefrontal cortex hypoactivation, and hippocampal volume reduction as the most reliably replicated structural and functional findings in PTSD. At the neuroendocrine level, PTSD is characterized by a distinctive hypocortisolism profile that is empirically distinct from the cortisol patterns observed in major depression and in chronic stress conditions. Autonomic dysregulation – marked by sympathetic hyperactivation, parasympathetic withdrawal, and reduced heart rate variability – is well-documented across the literature and carries significant cardiovascular implications for affected individuals. Throughout this chapter, findings supported by meta-analyses and large controlled studies are carefully distinguished from those resting on smaller samples, preclinical animal models, or broader theoretical frameworks such as polyvagal theory. These theoretical frameworks are discussed as clinically useful interpretive tools rather than as firmly established empirical findings. This distinction is essential for maintaining scientific rigor while acknowledging the practical value of integrative models. Understanding these interconnected neurobiological mechanisms has direct and meaningful implications for trauma-informed clinical practice and for the continued development of targeted, mechanism-based interventions. Together, these insights illustrate how trauma fundamentally reshapes brain function, stress physiology, and bodily regulation in ways that demand careful, evidence-based therapeutic attention and ongoing investigation.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la melatonina frenar la neurodegeneración post‑COVID?
stories.headline: Melatonina como inhibidor de ferroptosis: posible terapia contra el envejecimiento cerebral post‑COVID
stories.finding: El artículo describe cómo la infección por COVID‑19 desencadena neuroinflamación, disrupción del hierro, acumulación de ROS y alteraciones circadianas que favorecen la ferroptosis, un tipo de muerte celular vinculada al envejecimiento cerebral acelerado. Asimismo, señala que la melatonina ha demostrado eficacia como inhibidor de ferroptosis, sugiriendo un potencial terapéutico para mitigar la neurodegeneración post‑COVID.
stories.takeaway: Si la melatonina puede bloquear la ferroptosis, podría emplearse para prevenir el deterioro cognitivo y los trastornos neuropsiquiátricos en sobrevivientes de COVID‑19, ofreciendo una intervención segura y basada en un regulador del sueño.
stories.paperTitle: Melatonin: a ferroptosis inhibitor with potential therapeutic efficacy for the post-COVID-19 trajectory of accelerated brain aging and neurodegeneration
stories.originalAbstract: The unprecedented pandemic of COVID-19 swept millions of lives in a short period, yet its menace continues among its survivors in the form of post-COVID syndrome. An exponentially growing number of COVID-19 survivors suffer from cognitive impairment, with compelling evidence of a trajectory of accelerated aging and neurodegeneration. The novel and enigmatic nature of this yet-to-unfold pathology demands extensive research seeking answers for both the molecular underpinnings and potential therapeutic targets. Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent cell death, is a strongly proposed underlying mechanism in post-COVID-19 aging and neurodegeneration discourse. COVID-19 incites neuroinflammation, iron dysregulation, reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, antioxidant system repression, renin-angiotensin system (RAS) disruption, and clock gene alteration. These events pave the way for ferroptosis, which shows its signature in COVID-19, premature aging, and neurodegenerative disorders. In the search for a treatment, melatonin shines as a promising ferroptosis inhibitor with its repeatedly reported safety and tolerability. According to various studies, melatonin has proven efficacy in attenuating the severity of certain COVID-19 manifestations, validating its reputation as an anti-viral compound. Melatonin has well-documented anti-aging properties and combating neurodegenerative-related pathologies. Melatonin can block the leading events of ferroptosis since it is an efficient anti-inflammatory, iron chelator, antioxidant, angiotensin II antagonist, and clock gene regulator. Therefore, we propose ferroptosis as the culprit behind the post-COVID-19 trajectory of aging and neurodegeneration and melatonin, a well-fitting ferroptosis inhibitor, as a potential treatment.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la flexibilidad psicológica proteger contra la depresión?
stories.headline: Flexibilidad psicológica y autocompasión amortiguan la relación entre vergüenza y depresión
stories.finding: En una muestra de 207 adultos con discapacidad física, la flexibilidad psicológica y la autocompasión predijeron negativamente la depresión, incluso después de controlar la vergüenza. Además, ambos constructos moderaron significativamente el efecto de la vergüenza sobre la depresión (p < .05).
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que intervenciones basadas en ACT y mindfulness que fortalezcan la flexibilidad psicológica y la autocompasión pueden reducir la vulnerabilidad a la depresión en personas con discapacidad, ofreciendo una vía clínica para mitigar el impacto del estigma interno.
stories.paperTitle: Psychological flexibility and self-compassion buffer the impact of shame on depression among adults with physical disabilities
stories.originalAbstract: Individuals with physical disabilities experience higher rates of depression relative to the general population. Shame is a central mechanism linking disability status to poor mental health outcomes, including depression. Psychological flexibility and self-compassion have been shown to change one's relationship to negative self-evaluations such as shame. The goal of this study was to determine if psychological flexibility and self-compassion negatively predict depression and buffer the impact of shame on depression in adults with physical disabilities. Adults with physical disabilities (n = 207) completed self-report measures of psychological flexibility, self-compassion, shame, and depression. Consistent with prediction, a series of multiple regressions indicated that psychological flexibility and self-compassion negatively predicted depression over and beyond shame, and they both mitigated the impact of shame on depression among adults with physical disabilities (all p's < .05). These results suggest that psychological flexibility and self-compassion enhancing treatments, such as mindfulness-based interventions and acceptance and commitment therapy may be helpful in improving the mental health and wellbeing of adults with physical disabilities.

stories.hook: ¿Puede el apoyo reducir el síndrome del impostor?
stories.headline: El apoyo universitario atenúa la relación entre pertenencia y el fenómeno del impostor
stories.finding: El estudio 1 reveló que la percepción de un entorno universitario de apoyo, junto con el apoyo emocional e instrumental, fortaleció la relación negativa entre el sentido de pertenencia y el fenómeno del impostor en estudiantes negros. Así, mayor apoyo incrementó el efecto protector de la pertenencia.
stories.takeaway: Fomentar entornos compasivos y redes de apoyo en la universidad puede disminuir el impostor, reforzando la autoestima de estudiantes minoritarios y orientando intervenciones psicológicas y políticas institucionales.
stories.paperTitle: Impostor Phenomenon: Context, Coping, and Consciousness
stories.originalAbstract: The impostor phenomenon (IP) is a widely recognized psychological construct characterized by persistent feelings of intellectual fraudulence despite evidence of competence and achievement. Although research has increasingly examined IP among minoritized populations, limited attention has been given to within-group variation among Black college students and the contextual factors that shape these experiences. Guided by the phenomenological variant of ecological systems theory (PVEST), this dissertation examined environmental, psychological, and sociocultural factors associated with IP among Black emerging adult college students. Using cross-sectional survey data from 163 Black college students, three studies examined relationships involving (a) belonging and IP, (b) IP and maladaptive perfectionism, and (c) racial discrimination and IP. Contextual, coping, and consciousness variables were examined as moderators of these relationships. Study 1 found that perceptions of a supportive university environment, emotional support, and instrumental support strengthened the negative relationship between belonging and IP. These findings suggest that belonging serves as a stronger protective factor against impostor feelings when students perceive their environments as affirming and have access to meaningful support. Parental racial barrier messages did not significantly moderate this relationship. Study 2 examined maladaptive perfectionism as a coping response to impostor feelings. Positive emotionality and hopeful purpose did not significantly moderate the relationship between IP and maladaptive perfectionism. Academic self-efficacy emerged as the only significant moderator; however, contrary to expectations, higher self-efficacy strengthened the relationship between IP and maladaptive perfectionism. These findings suggest that confidence in one's academic abilities may coexist with heightened performance pressure and perfectionistic coping. Study 3 examined the relationship between racial discrimination and IP. Critical action did not significantly moderate this association. However, critical reflection strengthened the relationship between discrimination and IP, indicating that students with greater awareness of systemic inequities reported a stronger association between discriminatory experiences and impostor feelings. Collectively, the findings suggest that impostor phenomenon among Black college students is shaped by a complex interaction of environmental, psychological, and sociocultural influences. The results highlight the importance of belonging, social support, discrimination, and meaning-making processes in understanding impostor experiences and underscore the need for institutional efforts that address both individual well-being and the broader conditions that influence students’ academic experiences.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la atención plena reducir el desgaste ocupacional?
stories.headline: Mindfulness mejora significativamente el bienestar psicológico de los profesionales de salud
stories.finding: Una revisión sistemática y meta‑análisis de 27 ensayos controlados aleatorizados mostró que las intervenciones basadas en mindfulness aumentaron el bienestar psicológico de los trabajadores sanitarios. El análisis utilizó diferencias medias estandarizadas y modelo de efectos aleatorios.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo respalda la incorporación de programas de atención plena en entornos clínicos para mitigar el burnout y potenciar la salud mental del personal, ofreciendo una intervención basada en evidencia con efectos comprobados.
stories.paperTitle: Effectiveness of mindfulness‐based interventions on the well‐being of healthcare workers: a systematic review and meta‐analysis
stories.originalAbstract: Background: Growing evidence attests to the efficacy of mindfulness-based interventions (MBIs), but their effectiveness for healthcare workers remains uncertain. Aims: To evaluate the evidence for MBIs in improving healthcare workers' psychological well-being. Methods: A systematic literature search was conducted on Medline, Embase, Cumulative Index for Nursing and Allied Health Literature, PsycINFO and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials up to 31 August 2022 using the keywords 'healthcare worker', 'doctor', 'nurse', 'allied health', 'mindfulness', 'wellness', 'workshop' and 'program'. Randomised controlled trials with a defined MBI focusing on healthcare workers and quantitative outcome measures related to subjective or psychological well-being were eligible for inclusion. R V.4.0.3 was used for data analysis, with the standardised mean difference as the primary outcome, employing DerSimonian and Laird's random effects model. Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation framework was used to evaluate the quality of evidence. Cochrane's Risk of Bias 2 tool was used to assess the risk of bias in the included studies. Results: A total of 27 studies with 2506 participants were included, mostly from the USA, involving various healthcare professions. MBIs such as stress reduction programmes, apps, meditation and training showed small to large effects on anxiety, burnout, stress, depression, psychological distress and job strain outcomes of the participants. Positive effects were also seen in self-compassion, empathy, mindfulness and well-being. However, long-term outcomes (1 month or longer postintervention) varied, and the effects were not consistently sustained. Conclusions: MBIs offer short-term benefits in reducing stress-related symptoms in healthcare workers. The review also highlights limitations such as intervention heterogeneity, reduced power in specific subgroup analyses and variable study quality. PROSPERO registration number: CRD42022353340.

stories.hook: ¿Cómo influyen los traumas infantiles en la satisfacción marital?
stories.headline: Los ACEs predicen significativamente menor satisfacción conyugal
stories.finding: El estudio con 150 matrimonios encontró una correlación negativa significativa entre experiencias adversas en la infancia (ACE) y la satisfacción marital (r = -0.479, p < .01). Además, el análisis de regresión confirmó que los ACE son un predictor de menor satisfacción conyugal.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo subraya la necesidad de integrar enfoques basados en trauma en la terapia de pareja, pues abordar experiencias infantiles adversas puede mejorar la satisfacción marital.
stories.paperTitle: Adverse Childhood Experiences and Marital Satisfaction: A Correlational Study of Emotional Residue in Adult Romantic Relationships
stories.originalAbstract: This study investigates the direct relationship between Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACEs) and marital satisfaction among young married adults, excluding the influence of sibling dynamics. Childhood adversities such as abuse, neglect, and household dysfunction can significantly affect emotional regulation and adult relationship satisfaction. Despite extensive research on the psychological consequences of ACEs, their direct impact on marital satisfaction remains underexplored. A quantitative cross-sectional design was employed, collecting data from 150 married participants using purposive sampling. Standardized instruments, including the ACE Questionnaire and Couples Satisfaction Index (CSI), were utilized. Correlations and regression analyses were performed using SPSS version 25, with reliability analysis confirming tool consistency. Findings revealed a significant negative correlation between ACEs and marital satisfaction (r = -0.479, p < .01). Regression analysis identified ACEs as a significant predictor of lower marital satisfaction. Marriage counselors should adopt trauma-informed approaches when addressing marital conflicts. Early intervention programs for individuals with ACE histories can enhance relational outcomes in adulthood.

stories.hook: ¿Pueden los avatares digitales impulsar el compromiso ambiental?
stories.headline: Avatares humanos digitales aumentan el compromiso proambiental mediante la participación climática
stories.finding: En un estudio con 476 chinos y 485 surcoreanos de la generación Y/Z, los indicadores de origen del avatar digital, los indicadores sociales del contenido y su congruencia impulsaron la persuasión del DHA. La participación climática medió esa persuasión hacia el compromiso proambiental, y la preocupación ambiental actuó como condición límite.
stories.takeaway: Demuestra que los avatares digitales son herramientas persuasivas capaces de fomentar el compromiso ambiental, ofreciendo una estrategia novedosa para intervenciones de cambio de comportamiento y campañas de salud pública basadas en la teoría CASA y la congruencia.
stories.paperTitle: Digital human avatars as virtual influencers shape climate engagement and pro-environmental commitment
stories.originalAbstract: Nurturing pro-environmental commitment among consumers is crucial for mitigating climate change, as commitment is a pledge that precedes and predicts behavior. Given the criticality of the climate crisis and the urgent need for climate action, fostering commitment is vital for future behavioral change. Despite the potential of digital human avatars ( DHAs ) as virtual influencers alternative to human influencers in advocating environmental causes, empirical evidence regarding their effectiveness remains limited. In response, this research integrates computers as social actors ( CASA ) paradigm with congruity theory to investigate how DHAs can promote pro-environmental commitment through climate engagement as a mediating mechanism. Data were collected from 476 Chinese and 485 South Koreans from the same generational cohorts (Generations Y and Z) and analyzed using partial least squares path modeling. Results show that DHA-related source cues, content-related social cues, and DHA-content congruence are the key drivers of DHA persuasiveness, with climate engagement operating as a mediator that facilitates pro-environmental commitment while environmental concern serves as a boundary condition. These insights, in turn, contribute to environmental advocacy strategies aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 13 (SDG 13) on climate action.

stories.hook: ¿El conocimiento sobre desperdicio aumenta la propensión a desechar?
stories.headline: El conocimiento y la preocupación por el desperdicio aumentan la propensión a desechar alimentos
stories.finding: En una muestra de 672 encuestados de la República Checa, la conciencia del desperdicio y la preocupación por su costo se asociaron con mayor propensión a desechar alimentos, explicada por disonancia cognitiva. Además, la frecuencia de compra presenta una relación no lineal, indicando una frecuencia óptima para gestionar stocks.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo subraya la importancia de intervenciones que aumenten la conciencia sobre el desperdicio y reduzcan la disonancia cognitiva, así como la promoción de patrones de compra óptimos para disminuir el desperdicio alimentario, con implicaciones directas para políticas de sostenibilidad y salud pública.
stories.paperTitle: Food Waste Unveiled: Exploring Consumer Attitudes, Habits, and the Path to Sustainable Food Consumption
stories.originalAbstract: This study enriches the current state of knowledge presented in the literature review by investigating how the propensity to waste food is influenced by people's views on food waste, frequency of food purchases, and individual habits related to environmentally sustainable household practices. Binary logistic regression modelling in hierarchical form was developed from 672 completed questionnaires representing the population of the Czech Republic aged 15 and over. The research shows that the propensity to waste food is higher among individuals who are aware of their food waste and concerned about its cost, which can be explained by cognitive dissonance. The phenomenon of forgetting to consume food before it spoils is identified as an important economic reason for food waste, attributed to time inconsistency and imperfect information processing. The frequency of food purchases is found to have a nonlinear relationship with food waste, suggesting an optimal purchase frequency at which individuals can effectively manage their food stocks. Individuals who frequently bring their own bags to the supermarket and regularly sort their waste have lower levels of food waste, driven by pro-environmental behaviour, mindfulness, and adherence to social norms. The study provides practical insights such as educating the public about the environmental impact of food waste, tailoring communication strategies to address cognitive dissonance, developing community programmes that emphasise the social and moral aspects of reducing food waste and fostering a collective sense of responsibility, and implementing economic incentives or penalties to align economic behaviours with environmental and moral values regarding food waste.

stories.headline: El confinamiento francés intensifica dinámicas de duelo y revela resiliencia
stories.finding: Se entrevistaron a 31 personas que habían perdido a un ser querido, divididas en dos grupos según si la pérdida ocurrió durante el primer confinamiento o fuera de él. El análisis con ALCESTE mostró diferencias claras en las dinámicas de duelo y la aparición de mecanismos de resiliencia específicos en el grupo del confinamiento.
stories.takeaway: Comprender cómo el contexto de crisis modifica el proceso de duelo permite diseñar intervenciones más efectivas y políticas de apoyo que fomenten la resiliencia y reduzcan el sufrimiento psicológico.
stories.paperTitle: Impact of French lockdowns on bereavement experiences: Insight from ALCESTE analysis revealing psychological resilience and distinct grief dynamics amidst COVID ‐19
stories.originalAbstract: At the beginning of 2020, the entire world was shocked by a global health emergency. According to the literature, fear, high mortality and health restrictions had significant psychological consequences on the population. This study evaluates the French lockdown's impact on the grieving process and how people worked through their grief. Two semi-structured interviews were conducted with 31 participants who had lost a loved one between March 2020, June, and September 2021 (T0) and 6 months later (T1). Subsequently, they were divided into two groups: those who lost someone during the first lockdown (Group 1) and those who lost someone outside the lockdown periods (Group 2). The interviews were analysed using the ALCESTE software, a statistical analysis tool for textual data based on word co-occurrences. This research significantly advances the understanding of bereavement during crises, providing new perspectives and practical insights for policymakers, healthcare professionals and support organisations. Its methodological innovation and detailed analysis contribute to the ongoing discussion on grief and resilience in challenging circumstances. Ultimately, this study lays the foundation for improved support and intervention strategies tailored to the needs of bereaved individuals during crises.

stories.hook: ¿Cuáles son los riesgos ocultos del ADHD?
stories.headline: ADHD aumenta riesgos de salud mental, física y social
stories.finding: La revisión umbrella analizó 125 revisiones extraídas de 16,675 registros, mostrando que el ADHD (prevalencia hasta 5 %) se asocia a mayor riesgo de depresión, obesidad, encarcelamiento y divorcio, entre otros resultados adversos. La mayoría de las revisiones fueron de calidad buena o moderada.
stories.takeaway: Este compendio evidencia la necesidad de intervenciones integrales que aborden no solo los síntomas de inatención, sino también las consecuencias psicosociales del ADHD.
stories.paperTitle: The impacts associated with having ADHD: an umbrella review
stories.originalAbstract: Introduction: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) affects up to 5% of the population and is characterised by symptoms of impulsivity, hyperactivity and inattention. These symptoms are significantly impairing and carry additional risks for children and adults with ADHD, including negative mental health (e.g. depression), physical health (e.g. obesity) and societal outcomes (e.g. imprisonment, divorce). Very few studies have attempted to synthesise these risks in one publication due to the breadth of evidence published on the adverse outcomes of ADHD. Methods: An umbrella review was performed to identify reviews (systematic, meta-analysis and narrative) that investigate the risks arising from having ADHD. We conducted a narrative synthesis of the findings and conducted a quality review of the included publications. Results: Upon searching five databases, 16,675 records were identified. Of these, 125 reviews met the criteria for inclusion. A narrative synthesis of these findings highlighted three key domains of risks associated with ADHD: mental health, physical health, social and lifestyle. Most reviews were of good and moderate quality. Discussion: This review highlights the many risks associated with having ADHD, beyond its three key symptom domains and the impact of the condition on daily functioning. Registration: International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO CRD42023404073).

stories.hook: ¿Cómo negocian madres la autonomía en la dermatitis atópica?
stories.headline: Maternidad y autonomía: dinámicas familiares frente a la dermatitis atópica
stories.finding: El estudio cualitativo con quince madres de adolescentes con dermatitis atópica reveló dos temas principales: la negociación del cuidado y la autonomía dentro de la relación madre‑adolescente, y la distribución asimétrica del cuidado entre padres, que afecta la relación madre‑padre.
stories.takeaway: Comprender estas dinámicas permite a profesionales de salud diseñar intervenciones que favorezcan la autonomía del adolescente y la colaboración parental, mejorando la adherencia al tratamiento y el bienestar familiar.
stories.paperTitle: Exploring mothers' perspectives of family caregiving dynamics in adolescent atopic dermatitis: A qualitative study from Spain
stories.originalAbstract: PURPOSE: The aim of this study was to explore mothers' experiences of caring for adolescents with atopic dermatitis, focusing on caregiving dynamics within the family and their implications for mother-father-adolescent relationships. DESIGN AND METHODS: A qualitative descriptive study was carried out. Mothers of adolescents aged 12-17 years with atopic dermatitis were recruited using purposive sampling from dermatology departments in two public hospitals in north-western Spain. Semi-structured interviews were audio-recorded and transcribed verbatim. A thematic analysis was conducted. RESULTS: Fifteen mothers participated. Two themes were identified: (1) Negotiating care and autonomy in mother-adolescent relationships in the context of atopic dermatitis, and (2) Asymmetrical parental caregiving in adolescents with atopic dermatitis and its implications for mother-father relationships. Mothers described caregiving as an evolving responsibility, with adolescents gradually assuming self-care while mothers managed practical, cognitive and emotional aspects of treatment. Caregiving was negotiated within mother-adolescent relationships, with closeness and tension around autonomy, adherence and flare-up management. Fathers' limited involvement was perceived as contributing to asymmetrical caregiving, maternal burden, and changes in couple relationships and family functioning. CONCLUSION: Mothers described caregiving as a relational and negotiated process within family life, characterised by gendered expectations and asymmetrical responsibilities associated with maternal burden, emotional strain, and changes in couple relationships, sibling experiences and family organisation. PRACTICE IMPLICATIONS: Nursing care should adopt a family-centred approach that recognises asymmetrical caregiving roles, addresses maternal burden and promotes father and family involvement. Supporting communication and adolescents' progressive self-care may improve family functioning and well-being.

stories.hook: ¿Por qué el cerebro elimina demasiadas sinapsis en esquizofrenia?
stories.headline: Exceso de poda sináptica contribuye a déficits cognitivos en la esquizofrenia
stories.finding: Los autores revisan evidencia de que la esquizofrenia se origina por interrupciones neurodesarrollamentales que provocan una poda sináptica excesiva durante la adolescencia. Estudios moleculares vinculan este proceso a la activación del sistema del complemento y a la microglía, lo que se asocia con déficits cognitivos y síntomas psicóticos.
stories.takeaway: Reconocer la poda sináptica excesiva como mecanismo central abre la puerta a intervenciones que modulen el sistema del complemento o la actividad microglial, ofreciendo nuevas estrategias terapéuticas para prevenir o mitigar los déficits cognitivos en la esquizofrenia.
stories.paperTitle: On the prefrontal cortex neurodevelopmental disruptions and excessive synaptic pruning in schizophrenia: recent developments and challenges
stories.journal: The Egyptian Journal of Neurology Psychiatry and Neurosurgery
stories.originalAbstract: Abstract Schizophrenia is a complex chronic mental disorder, revealed in adolescence or early adulthood, and is manifested by cognitive, emotional, and behavioral abnormalities. Owing to its complex nature and poor prognosis methods, multiple hypothesis have been proposed on the origin of schizophrenia. The neurodevelopmental hypothesis posits that schizophrenia arises from the intricate interplay of genetic, environmental, and neurobiological factors. These in turn lead to a considerable disruption in brain development during critical periods, particularly in fetal growth, early childhood, and adolescence. Disruptions in neural connectivity, both at the synaptic and circuit level, can lead to structural and functional abnormalities in brain, including gray matter reductions, cortical thinning, and white matter microstructural deficits. Excessive synaptic pruning, a self-activated natural process critical for efficient neural network refinement, appears to be overactivated in schizophrenia, contributing to cognitive deficits and psychotic symptoms. Molecular and genetic studies implicate complement-mediated microglial pruning, dysregulated neurodevelopmental genes (e.g., DISC1, C4, OPCML), and immune signaling pathways as mechanistic drivers of these synaptic and structural alterations. Translational models using CRISPR-edited human iPSC-derived neurons and cerebral organoids recapitulate schizophrenia-associated phenotypes, including impaired dendritic morphology, reduced synaptic density, neurotransmitter imbalance, and heightened sensitivity to environmental stressors. Multimodal neuroimaging, synaptic density tracers, and computational modeling reveal early biomarkers of pathological pruning and neurovascular dysregulation, offering potential for risk stratification and early intervention. Integrating molecular, structural, and functional findings highlights adolescence as a critical window of vulnerability and points toward preventive strategies, such as modulation of immune signaling, synaptic maintenance, and circuit-level interventions. Understanding schizophrenia as a neurodevelopmental disorder provides a better framework linking genetic, cellular, and structural changes in neurobiological system, offering potential avenues for personalized medicine and early targeted therapeutic approaches. This narrative Review provides insights into neuroplasticity mechanisms associated with the pathophysiology of schizophrenia as a neurobiological illness, particularly in the context of excessive synaptic pruning, recent advances, and challenges.
